notes.client-openness: Client-side annotation code is open source under [BSD 2-Clause license](https://github.com/hypothesis/client) on GitHub. Browser extensions and annotation interface are fully open.
notes.server-components: Main web service ('h') is open source under [BSD 2-Clause license](https://github.com/hypothesis/h) but some infrastructure and service components remain proprietary.
notes.api-openness: [API](https://h.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api-reference/) is fully documented and open. Third-party developers can build integrations and alternative clients.
notes.contribution-model: Active open source community with contributions accepted through GitHub. [Developer documentation](https://h.readthedocs.io/) supports external development.
notes.licensing-clarity: Clear BSD licensing for open components. Mixed licensing model where core annotation functionality is open but some operational infrastructure is proprietary.

notes.offline: Hypothesis is a cloud-based annotation platform with no offline support. All annotations are stored on Hypothesis servers and require internet connection for access and synchronization.
notes.e2ee: No end-to-end encryption mentioned in documentation or [security overview](https://web.hypothes.is/help/security/). Data is transmitted over HTTPS but stored unencrypted on servers.
notes.bug-bounty: Hypothesis runs a responsible disclosure program through [security@hypothes.is](mailto:security@hypothes.is) but no formal bug bounty program with financial rewards.
notes.data-selling: According to their [privacy policy](https://web.hypothes.is/privacy/), Hypothesis does not sell user data. They are a non-profit organization focused on open annotation standards rather than commercial data exploitation.
notes.email-consent: Requires email for account creation. Users can control notification preferences for group activities and replies. Educational institutions can manage user data through administrative controls.
notes.spam-rate: Minimal promotional emails. Primarily sends notifications about annotation replies and group activities. Educational users report low spam rates.
notes.anonymous-data-collection: Collects usage analytics to improve the service. Public annotations are intentionally discoverable. Private groups and private annotations maintain privacy within defined boundaries.
notes.misuse: Strong commitment to educational and research use cases. Clear [terms of service](https://web.hypothes.is/terms-of-service/) prohibiting harassment and abuse. Active moderation for public annotations.

notes.bug-free: High uptime with [status page](https://status.hypothes.is/) showing infrastructure health. 13+ years of operation with established track record.
notes.uptime: Strong data integrity with annotations reliably preserved. Backed by institutional infrastructure and careful data management practices.
notes.performance: Good performance for annotation loading and synchronization. Minimal latency for collaborative features.
notes.sync-reliability: Reliable real-time synchronization across users in group annotations. Collaborative features work consistently.
notes.crash-free: Low bug frequency due to mature codebase and extensive testing in educational environments.
notes.platform-stability: Stable across all supported platforms with consistent experience. Well-maintained browser extensions.

notes.setup-ease: Extremely easy setup, especially for educational use. One-click browser extension installation. [Quick start guide](https://web.hypothes.is/quick-start-guide/) available.
notes.learning-curve: Minimal learning curve for basic annotation. Advanced features like groups require brief orientation.
notes.maintenance: Regular updates with active development on [GitHub](https://github.com/hypothesis). Responsive to security and compatibility issues.
notes.friction: Easy setup and learning curve for basic annotation. Advanced features require brief orientation.
notes.lms-integration: Seamless integration with major LMS platforms including Canvas, Blackboard, and Moodle through [LTI](https://web.hypothes.is/education/).

notes.email-support: Excellent support for educational users through [dedicated channels](https://web.hypothes.is/contact/). Responsive community support.
notes.community-support: Good community support through forums and discussions.
notes.documentation: Comprehensive [help documentation](https://web.hypothes.is/help/) and [developer docs](https://h.readthedocs.io/). Strong educational support materials.

notes.business-model: Non-profit organization with funding from foundations and educational institutions. Free for most users with [premium features](https://web.hypothes.is/education/) for institutions.
notes.export-capabilities: Strong export capabilities through [API](https://h.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api-reference/) and bulk download options. Supports data portability.
notes.self-hosting: Open source components allow self-hosting of core functionality, though full infrastructure requires technical expertise.
notes.data-portability: Excellent data portability through standardized formats and comprehensive API access.
notes.financial-stability: Stable funding model through educational partnerships and foundation grants. Strong institutional adoption provides sustainability.
notes.vendor-lock-in: Low vendor lock-in due to open source components, API access, and export capabilities. Open annotation standards support.

features.notes: No offline functionality available. Requires internet connection for all annotation and collaboration features.

notes.editor-support: Annotation editor supports basic formatting with limited markdown-like syntax for links, emphasis, and simple formatting.
notes.syntax-support: Supports links, italic/bold text, and basic formatting. No support for headers, code blocks, lists, or advanced markdown features.
notes.rendering: Annotations render with basic formatting applied. Links are clickable and emphasis is displayed correctly.
notes.import-export: Exported annotations maintain basic formatting but limited markdown compatibility for import to other tools.

notes.annotation-quality: Excellent PDF annotation capabilities through browser extension. Annotations are precisely anchored to PDF content.
notes.local-pdf-support: Works with PDFs opened in browser, including locally stored files. Supports both embedded and linked PDFs.
notes.annotation-types: Supports highlighting, note annotations, and page notes. Can anchor annotations to specific text passages in PDFs.
notes.sync-across-devices: PDF annotations sync across all devices and platforms. Collaborative PDF annotation works seamlessly.
notes.export-integration: PDF annotations accessible through API and export functions. Integrates well with educational workflows.
notes.educational-integration: Strong integration with educational PDF workflows. Used extensively in academic settings for collaborative reading.

notes.standalone-notes: Very limited standalone note creation. Platform is designed for annotation of existing content rather than original writing.
notes.note-quality: Annotation notes can be detailed with basic formatting, but no dedicated note-taking interface.
notes.organization: Notes exist as annotations tied to specific content. No separate note organization system.
notes.search-in-notes: Notes are searchable through annotation search interface. Full-text search across all annotation content.

notes.annotation-quality: Outstanding web annotation with precise text anchoring. Annotations survive page updates and dynamic content changes.
notes.page-compatibility: Works on virtually any web page including complex single-page applications, news sites, and academic content.
notes.context-preservation: Excellent context preservation with robust text anchoring that maintains annotation position even when page content changes.
notes.annotation-workflow: Seamless annotation workflow with highlighting, note-taking, and tagging in single interface.
notes.cross-browser-support: Consistent experience across Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and mobile browsers.
notes.collaboration-features: Real-time collaborative annotation with public/private options and group-based sharing.

notes.video-platform-support: Good support for annotating video pages on YouTube, Vimeo, and educational platforms. Can annotate video descriptions and surrounding content.
notes.timestamp-support: Limited timestamp annotation support. Can reference time points in notes but no automatic video position linking.
notes.educational-integration: Strong integration with educational video platforms used in online learning environments.
notes.collaborative-viewing: Group annotation capabilities work well for collaborative video analysis in educational settings.

notes.platform-support: Excellent support for annotating content shared on social media platforms and in online discussions.
notes.context-preservation: Maintains social context including author information, discussion threads, and original post links.
notes.collaborative-features: Strong collaborative annotation features enable group discussions around social media content.
notes.educational-use: Widely used in educational settings for analyzing social media content, online discussions, and digital literacy.

notes.tagging-system: Good tagging system for organizing annotations by topic, assignment, or research area.
notes.workflow-integration: Tagging integrated into annotation workflow, making categorization easy during content consumption.
notes.group-organization: Can organize content curation within groups for collaborative research and learning.
notes.search-integration: Tags integrate well with search functionality for retrieving curated content.

notes.group-system: Strong group-based organization allowing collaborative annotation collections. Groups can be public, private, or restricted.
notes.tag-organization: Personal annotation organization through tagging system. Can filter and organize by multiple tag criteria.
notes.collaborative-curation: Groups enable collaborative curation of annotated content for educational and research purposes.
notes.discovery-features: Can discover public annotations and groups related to topics of interest.

notes.search-scope: Comprehensive search across all annotations, tags, groups, and users. Can search within specific groups or across all public content.
notes.search-quality: Good full-text search with relevance ranking. Finds content within annotation text and highlighted passages.
notes.filtering-options: Advanced filtering by group, user, date range, and tags. Can combine multiple search criteria.
notes.api-access: Search functionality available through [API](https://h.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api-reference/) for programmatic access.

notes.annotation-references: Can reference other annotations through replies and mentions, but no automatic backlinking.
notes.user-mentions: Can mention other users in annotations, creating notification-based connections.
notes.link-visualization: No visual representation of connections between annotations or knowledge graph features.
notes.relationship-discovery: Limited relationship discovery - connections mainly through shared tags and group participation.

notes.threaded-discussions: Excellent threaded discussion system with replies to annotations creating rich collaborative conversations.
notes.notification-system: Robust notification system for replies, mentions, and group activity. Keeps users engaged in ongoing discussions.
notes.moderation-features: Good moderation capabilities for group administrators and public annotation oversight.
notes.educational-collaboration: Widely used in educational settings for peer discussion, instructor feedback, and collaborative analysis.
notes.real-time-features: Real-time updates when other users add comments or replies to shared content.
